spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m6p6t4 ----
\* A print-shop job spooler: printers acquire time-bounded leases on queued
\* jobs. A lease that outlives its expiry tick is reclaimed by the clock
\* itself (atomically, on the same step the clock passes it), so a printer
\* whose lease has gone stale can never be found still holding a job.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Jobs, Printers, NoPrinter, MaxTime, MaxCap, LeaseDuration

ASSUME NoPrinter \notin Printers

VARIABLES status, owner, expiry, clock, capacity

vars == <<status, owner, expiry, clock, capacity>>

Cap(x) == IF x > MaxTime THEN MaxTime ELSE x

TypeOK ==
  /\ status \in [Jobs -> {"queued", "leased", "done"}]
  /\ owner \in [Jobs -> Printers \cup {NoPrinter}]
  /\ expiry \in [Jobs -> 0..MaxTime]
  /\ clock \in 0..MaxTime
  /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

\* SAFETY PROPERTY: a job that is leased always has a temporally valid,
\* named-printer owner -- never a stale (expired) or unauthorized holder.
LeaseValidity ==
  \A j \in Jobs :
    status[j] = "leased" => (clock <= expiry[j] /\ owner[j] \in Printers)

Init ==
  /\ status = [j \in Jobs |-> "queued"]
  /\ owner = [j \in Jobs |-> NoPrinter]
  /\ expiry = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ capacity = MaxCap

ActiveLeases == Cardinality({j \in Jobs : status[j] = "leased"})

Claim(p, j) ==
  /\ status[j] = "queued"
  /\ ActiveLeases < capacity
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![j] = "leased"]
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = p]
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![j] = Cap(clock + LeaseDuration)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, capacity>>

Renew(p, j) ==
  /\ status[j] = "leased"
  /\ owner[j] = p
  /\ clock <= expiry[j]
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![j] = Cap(clock + LeaseDuration)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, owner, clock, capacity>>

Complete(p, j) ==
  /\ status[j] = "leased"
  /\ owner[j] = p
  /\ clock <= expiry[j]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![j] = "done"]
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = NoPrinter]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, clock, capacity>>

\* The wall clock advances and, in the same step, reclaims any lease whose
\* expiry has just passed -- so no observable state ever shows a stale owner.
Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxTime
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ status' = [j \in Jobs |->
        IF status[j] = "leased" /\ expiry[j] <= clock' THEN "queued" ELSE status[j]]
  /\ owner' = [j \in Jobs |->
        IF status[j] = "leased" /\ expiry[j] <= clock' THEN NoPrinter ELSE owner[j]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, capacity>>

\* Operators may re-provision the shop's concurrent-lease capacity at any
\* time (the runtime twist); this also keeps some action always enabled.
SetCapacity(newCap) ==
  /\ newCap \in 1..MaxCap
  /\ capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, owner, expiry, clock>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Printers, j \in Jobs : Claim(p, j) \/ Renew(p, j) \/ Complete(p, j)
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E newCap \in 1..MaxCap : SetCapacity(newCap)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Jobs = {j1, j2, j3}
  Printers = {p1, p2}
  NoPrinter = none
  MaxTime = 4
  MaxCap = 2
  LeaseDuration = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT LeaseValidity
nl:
A small print shop runs a job spooler in front of a bank of printers. Jobs arrive queued and waiting. A printer may CLAIM a queued job as long as the shop's currently configured concurrent-lease capacity has not been reached; claiming hands the printer a time-bounded lease on the job and stamps an expiry tick. While a printer still holds a valid (unexpired) lease on its job it may RENEW the lease, pushing the expiry further into the future, or COMPLETE the job, marking it done and releasing the lease. The shop's wall clock TICKs forward one unit at a time, and whenever the clock passes a job's recorded expiry, that reclamation happens in the very same tick: the job is put back in the queue and its owner is cleared, so no printer is ever left holding a job past its lease. Finally, the shop's owner may RECONFIGURE the printers' shared capacity at any time, raising or lowering how many jobs may be concurrently leased out.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a job is recorded as leased, its lease has not yet expired and its owner is one of the shop's actual printers, so no stale or unauthorized participant is ever found holding a job.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m1p4t4 ----
\* An air-traffic runway allocator: controllers sit on a ring and pass a
\* single token around it. Only the current token holder may clear a
\* waiting aircraft onto the runway, and the shared runway bank never
\* holds more aircraft at once than its (runtime-adjustable) capacity.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumControllers, MaxCap

Ring == 1..NumControllers

Next1(i) == IF i = NumControllers THEN 1 ELSE i + 1

VARIABLES token, using, requesting, capacity

vars == <<token, using, requesting, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Ring
  /\ using \subseteq Ring
  /\ requesting \subseteq Ring
  /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

\* SAFETY PROPERTY (bounded capacity is never exceeded): the number of
\* aircraft occupying the runway bank never exceeds the current capacity.
RunwayCapacityOK == Cardinality(using) <= capacity

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ using = {}
  /\ requesting = {}
  /\ capacity = MaxCap

\* An aircraft controlled by i calls in and asks for a landing slot.
Request(i) ==
  /\ i \notin requesting
  /\ i \notin using
  /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {i}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, using, capacity>>

\* Only the controller currently holding the token may clear its waiting
\* aircraft onto the runway bank, and only if there is spare capacity.
Enter ==
  /\ token \in requesting
  /\ token \notin using
  /\ Cardinality(using) < capacity
  /\ using' = using \cup {token}
  /\ requesting' = requesting \ {token}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, capacity>>

\* Any aircraft already on the runway may complete its landing and leave.
Exit(i) ==
  /\ i \in using
  /\ using' = using \ {i}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, requesting, capacity>>

\* The token is unconditionally handed to the next controller in the ring;
\* this keeps the ring circulating regardless of runway or request state.
Pass ==
  /\ token' = Next1(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<using, requesting, capacity>>

\* Airport operations may re-provision how many runways are open at once,
\* but never below the number of aircraft already occupying the bank.
SetCapacity(newCap) ==
  /\ newCap \in 1..MaxCap
  /\ newCap >= Cardinality(using)
  /\ capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, using, requesting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Ring : Request(i)
  \/ Enter
  \/ \E i \in Ring : Exit(i)
  \/ Pass
  \/ \E newCap \in 1..MaxCap : SetCapacity(newCap)

\* LIVENESS PROPERTY: the token is never stuck on one controller -- every
\* controller in the ring eventually holds it.
TokenReachesAll == \A i \in Ring : <>(token = i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Pass)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  NumControllers = 3
  MaxCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT RunwayCapacityOK

PROPERTY TokenReachesAll
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator manages a small bank of runways shared by several controllers arranged in a ring. A single token circulates around the ring, and only whichever controller currently holds the token is allowed to clear its own waiting aircraft onto the runway bank. The actions are: REQUEST, where a controller's aircraft calls in and joins the waiting list for a landing slot; ENTER, where the controller holding the token clears its waiting aircraft onto the runway bank, but only if the bank has spare capacity; EXIT, where any aircraft already on the runway bank finishes its landing roll-out and clears the bank; PASS, where the token is handed unconditionally to the next controller around the ring, regardless of how many aircraft are waiting or landed; and RECONFIGURE, where airport operations may raise or lower the bank's capacity at any time, though never below the number of aircraft already sitting on it. The token never lingers with an aircraft that already has its slot, and it keeps moving purely on its own schedule.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of aircraft occupying the runway bank at any moment never exceeds the currently configured capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The token is never stuck on a single controller forever -- every controller in the ring eventually gets to hold it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m6p2t2 ----
\* A university course-registration system: two independently operated
\* registration instances (e.g. two campuses) draw seat holds from one
\* shared seat pool for a single course. A hold is a lease: it gives a
\* student's instance temporary ownership of a seat, but an unconfirmed
\* hold may time out at any moment and the seat silently returns to the
\* shared pool. No seat is ever created or destroyed by any of this.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS TotalSeats

VARIABLES pool, heldA, heldB, confirmedA, confirmedB

vars == <<pool, heldA, heldB, confirmedA, confirmedB>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ pool \in 0..TotalSeats
  /\ heldA \in 0..TotalSeats
  /\ heldB \in 0..TotalSeats
  /\ confirmedA \in 0..TotalSeats
  /\ confirmedB \in 0..TotalSeats

\* SAFETY PROPERTY: every seat is always accounted for in exactly one of
\* the shared pool, an instance's held (leased) count, or its confirmed
\* count -- the total number of seats is conserved.
SeatsConserved == pool + heldA + heldB + confirmedA + confirmedB = TotalSeats

Init ==
  /\ pool = TotalSeats
  /\ heldA = 0
  /\ heldB = 0
  /\ confirmedA = 0
  /\ confirmedB = 0

\* Instance A leases a seat out of the shared pool for a student to hold.
HoldA ==
  /\ pool > 0
  /\ pool' = pool - 1
  /\ heldA' = heldA + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldB, confirmedA, confirmedB>>

\* The student confirms enrollment before the lease expires.
ConfirmA ==
  /\ heldA > 0
  /\ heldA' = heldA - 1
  /\ confirmedA' = confirmedA + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, heldB, confirmedB>>

\* An unconfirmed hold on instance A can time out at any moment, and the
\* seat it leased is returned to the shared pool.
ExpireA ==
  /\ heldA > 0
  /\ heldA' = heldA - 1
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldB, confirmedA, confirmedB>>

\* A confirmed student on instance A drops the course, freeing the seat.
DropA ==
  /\ confirmedA > 0
  /\ confirmedA' = confirmedA - 1
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldA, heldB, confirmedB>>

\* Instance B leases a seat out of the same shared pool.
HoldB ==
  /\ pool > 0
  /\ pool' = pool - 1
  /\ heldB' = heldB + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldA, confirmedA, confirmedB>>

ConfirmB ==
  /\ heldB > 0
  /\ heldB' = heldB - 1
  /\ confirmedB' = confirmedB + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, heldA, confirmedA>>

ExpireB ==
  /\ heldB > 0
  /\ heldB' = heldB - 1
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldA, confirmedA, confirmedB>>

DropB ==
  /\ confirmedB > 0
  /\ confirmedB' = confirmedB - 1
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldA, heldB, confirmedA>>

Next ==
  \/ HoldA \/ ConfirmA \/ ExpireA \/ DropA
  \/ HoldB \/ ConfirmB \/ ExpireB \/ DropB

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  TotalSeats = 5

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatsConserved
nl:
A university runs course registration for one popular course through two independently operated registration instances -- think of them as two campus portals -- that both draw seats from a single shared seat pool for that course. On instance A, a student can HOLDA a seat, which leases one seat out of the shared pool into instance A's held count. That hold is not permanent: at any time before the student finalizes their enrollment, the hold can EXPIREA, silently timing out and returning the seat to the shared pool so it is available to either instance again. If instead the student acts in time, they CONFIRMA their registration, moving the seat from instance A's held count into its confirmed count. A student who later changes their mind can DROPA a confirmed seat, returning it to the shared pool. Instance B offers a mirror-image set of actions on the same shared pool: HOLDB, EXPIREB, CONFIRMB, and DROPB, operating entirely independently of instance A's bookkeeping but competing for the same underlying seats.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every moment, every seat is accounted for in exactly one place -- the shared pool, one instance's held (leased) count, or one instance's confirmed count -- so seats are never created or destroyed by holding, confirming, expiring, or dropping.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m0p6t3 ----
\* A car-wash conveyor line: several wash arms use optimistic locking to
\* finish washing the car currently in front of the belt. An arm reads the
\* belt's version, works, and only its commit counts if the belt hasn't
\* moved since; otherwise its attempt is stale and must be abandoned and
\* re-read. An arm may be slow (it can dawdle indefinitely) but it is
\* never assumed to have failed outright -- it always eventually retries.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Stations, MaxVersion

Cap(x) == IF x > MaxVersion THEN MaxVersion ELSE x

VARIABLES version, cached, washing, appliedVersion

vars == <<version, cached, washing, appliedVersion>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
  /\ cached \in [Stations -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ washing \in [Stations -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ appliedVersion \in [Stations -> 0..MaxVersion]

\* SAFETY PROPERTY: an arm can only ever record a finished wash for the
\* belt version it actually validated against -- it never gets credit for
\* a version that lies beyond (ahead of) the belt's true current version.
AuthorizedCommit == \A s \in Stations : appliedVersion[s] <= version

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ cached = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
  /\ washing = [s \in Stations |-> FALSE]
  /\ appliedVersion = [s \in Stations |-> 0]

\* An idle arm reads the belt's current version and starts a wash attempt.
Read(s) ==
  /\ ~washing[s]
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![s] = version]
  /\ washing' = [washing EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, appliedVersion>>

\* The arm finishes and its commit is accepted only because the belt has
\* not moved since it read -- a stale (unauthorized) commit is impossible
\* by construction, and finishing a car is what moves the belt forward.
Commit(s) ==
  /\ washing[s]
  /\ cached[s] = version
  /\ washing' = [washing EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ appliedVersion' = [appliedVersion EXCEPT ![s] = version]
  /\ version' = Cap(version + 1)
  /\ UNCHANGED cached

\* The arm finishes but discovers the belt moved on since it read; its
\* result is discarded and it must retry with a fresh read.
Abort(s) ==
  /\ washing[s]
  /\ cached[s] # version
  /\ washing' = [washing EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, cached, appliedVersion>>

\* A car can also be pulled off the line without any arm finishing it
\* (e.g. rejected upstream), which likewise advances the belt and can
\* make any in-progress read go stale.
Skip ==
  /\ version' = Cap(version + 1)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cached, washing, appliedVersion>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Stations : Read(s) \/ Commit(s) \/ Abort(s)
  \/ Skip

\* LIVENESS PROPERTY: an arm that has fallen behind (its cached read no
\* longer matches the belt) is not stuck forever -- it always eventually
\* catches back up to the belt's current version.
CatchesUp == \A s \in Stations : (cached[s] # version) ~> (cached[s] = version)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ (\A s \in Stations : WF_vars(Read(s)) /\ WF_vars(Commit(s) \/ Abort(s)))

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Stations = {s1, s2}
  MaxVersion = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT AuthorizedCommit

PROPERTY CatchesUp
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has several wash arms stationed along the belt, each using optimistic locking to finish washing whatever car currently sits in front of it. The actions are: READ, where an idle arm reads the belt's current version number and begins a wash attempt; COMMIT, where an arm that has finished washing checks whether the belt's version still matches what it read -- if so its work is accepted, the car is considered done, and the belt advances to the next version; ABORT, where an arm that has finished washing discovers the belt moved on while it worked, so its result is discarded and it must go back and read again; and SKIP, where a car is pulled off the line without being washed at all (for example it was flagged upstream), which also advances the belt and can make any arm's in-progress read go stale. An arm can be slow -- it may take arbitrarily long between reading and finishing -- but it is never assumed to break down or vanish, so it always eventually tries again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: An arm never gets credit for having finished a belt version that is still ahead of (later than) the belt's actual current version -- no stale or unauthorized commit is ever recorded as if it were current.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: An arm that has fallen behind the belt's current version is never stuck permanently behind -- it always eventually catches back up so its cached version matches the belt's current version.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m9p2t4 ----
\* A hospital operating-room scheduler: patients move through waiting,
\* surgery, recovery, and finally discharge, while hospital administration
\* may reconfigure how many operating rooms are active at once. Each
\* reconfiguration is stamped with a fresh epoch number, but no patient is
\* ever created or destroyed by any of this -- everyone is always in
\* exactly one of the four stages.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS TotalPatients, MaxCap, MaxEpoch

CapE(x) == IF x > MaxEpoch THEN MaxEpoch ELSE x

VARIABLES waiting, inSurgery, recovery, home, epoch, capacity

vars == <<waiting, inSurgery, recovery, home, epoch, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ waiting \in 0..TotalPatients
  /\ inSurgery \in 0..TotalPatients
  /\ recovery \in 0..TotalPatients
  /\ home \in 0..TotalPatients
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

\* SAFETY PROPERTY: every patient is always accounted for in exactly one
\* of the four stages -- nobody is ever created or lost as they move
\* through the schedule or as capacity is reconfigured underneath them.
PatientsConserved == waiting + inSurgery + recovery + home = TotalPatients

Init ==
  /\ waiting = TotalPatients
  /\ inSurgery = 0
  /\ recovery = 0
  /\ home = 0
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ capacity = MaxCap

\* A waiting patient is admitted into an operating room, but only if the
\* room bank has not reached the currently configured capacity.
Admit ==
  /\ waiting > 0
  /\ inSurgery < capacity
  /\ waiting' = waiting - 1
  /\ inSurgery' = inSurgery + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<recovery, home, epoch, capacity>>

\* A patient's operation finishes and they move to post-op recovery.
FinishSurgery ==
  /\ inSurgery > 0
  /\ inSurgery' = inSurgery - 1
  /\ recovery' = recovery + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, home, epoch, capacity>>

\* A recovered patient is discharged home.
Discharge ==
  /\ recovery > 0
  /\ recovery' = recovery - 1
  /\ home' = home + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, inSurgery, epoch, capacity>>

\* Hospital administration reconfigures how many operating rooms are open
\* at once (the runtime capacity twist), stamping a new epoch each time.
\* Patients already mid-operation are never displaced by a reconfiguration.
Reconfigure(newCap) ==
  /\ newCap \in 1..MaxCap
  /\ epoch' = CapE(epoch + 1)
  /\ capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, inSurgery, recovery, home>>

Next ==
  \/ Admit
  \/ FinishSurgery
  \/ Discharge
  \/ \E newCap \in 1..MaxCap : Reconfigure(newCap)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  TotalPatients = 4
  MaxCap = 2
  MaxEpoch = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT PatientsConserved
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler tracks every patient on today's surgical list as they move through four stages: waiting, in surgery, in recovery, and discharged home. The actions are: ADMIT, where a waiting patient is brought into an operating room, but only if the number of patients currently in surgery has not reached the hospital's currently configured operating-room capacity; FINISHSURGERY, where a patient's operation completes and they move into post-op recovery; DISCHARGE, where a recovered patient is sent home; and RECONFIGURE, where hospital administration changes how many operating rooms are open at once, stamping the change with a fresh epoch number each time this happens -- but a reconfiguration never displaces a patient who is already mid-operation, it only changes how many new patients can be admitted going forward. Capacity can be raised or lowered at any time as staffing and room availability change.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every patient is always accounted for in exactly one of the four stages -- waiting, in surgery, in recovery, or discharged home -- so no patient is ever created or lost, no matter how many times capacity is reconfigured.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m3p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers1, Controllers2, PoolCap, NoLeader

ASSUME NoLeader \notin (Controllers1 \cup Controllers2)

Homes == {1, 2}
Ctrls(i) == IF i = 1 THEN Controllers1 ELSE Controllers2

VARIABLES leader, alive, held, pool

vars == <<leader, alive, held, pool>>

\* leader[i] names the current leader controller of home i (or NoLeader); alive[i]
\* is the set of that home's controllers currently reachable (not crashed).
TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in [Homes -> Controllers1 \cup Controllers2 \cup {NoLeader}]
    /\ \A i \in Homes : leader[i] \in Ctrls(i) \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ alive \in [Homes -> SUBSET (Controllers1 \cup Controllers2)]
    /\ \A i \in Homes : alive[i] \subseteq Ctrls(i)
    /\ held \in [Homes -> 0..PoolCap]
    /\ pool \in 0..PoolCap

\* Every session credit is always free in the shared pool or held by one home's leader.
Conservation == pool + held[1] + held[2] = PoolCap

Init ==
    /\ leader = [i \in Homes |-> CHOOSE c \in Ctrls(i) : TRUE]
    /\ alive = [i \in Homes |-> Ctrls(i)]
    /\ held = [i \in Homes |-> 0]
    /\ pool = PoolCap

Elect(i) ==
    /\ leader[i] = NoLeader
    /\ alive[i] # {}
    /\ \E c \in alive[i] : leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, held, pool>>

\* A silent crash: the leader vanishes from the reachable set and any credits
\* it held fail safe back to the shared pool.
Crash(i) ==
    /\ leader[i] # NoLeader
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![i] = alive[i] \ {leader[i]}]
    /\ pool' = pool + held[i]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = NoLeader]

Reboot(i) ==
    /\ \E c \in Ctrls(i) \ alive[i] :
         alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![i] = alive[i] \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, held, pool>>

Borrow(i) ==
    /\ leader[i] # NoLeader
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = held[i] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

Return(i) ==
    /\ held[i] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = held[i] - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

Next == \E i \in Homes : Elect(i) \/ Crash(i) \/ Reboot(i) \/ Borrow(i) \/ Return(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ (\A i \in Homes : WF_vars(Elect(i)))
    /\ (\A i \in Homes : WF_vars(Reboot(i)))

\* A home whose leader slot is currently empty eventually gets a new leader.
Failover == \A i \in Homes : (leader[i] = NoLeader) ~> (leader[i] # NoLeader)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers1 = {c1, c2}
    Controllers2 = {c3, c4}
    NoLeader = NoLeader
    PoolCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conservation
PROPERTY Failover
nl:
This spec models a smart-home door lock network split across two independent homes, each with its own set of lock controllers. Within each home, exactly one controller at a time serves as the leader responsible for granting temporary "unlock sessions" to residents; if the leader's controller crashes, the home fails over by electing a replacement leader from among its still-reachable controllers. Both homes draw their unlock sessions from a single shared pool of session credits maintained by the central smart-home hub (the twist: two independent home networks share one pool). The full action set is: Elect1 / Elect2, where a home whose leader slot is empty and that still has at least one reachable controller promotes one of those controllers to leader; Crash1 / Crash2, where the current leader controller of a home fails silently, vacating the leader slot, dropping that controller from the reachable set, and immediately returning to the shared pool any session credits that controller was holding (a crashed lock fails safe and releases its holds); Reboot1 / Reboot2, where a previously crashed controller comes back online and rejoins its home's reachable set, making it eligible to be elected again; Borrow1 / Borrow2, where a home's current leader draws one credit from the shared pool to grant a resident an unlock session; and Return1 / Return2, where a home's leader gives back one credit it is currently holding to the shared pool once a session ends. No credit is ever created or destroyed: every credit is always either sitting free in the shared pool or held by exactly one of the two homes' leaders.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared pool's free credits plus the credits held by home 1's leader plus the credits held by home 2's leader must always equal the fixed total pool capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a home's leader slot becomes empty (after its leader crashes), that home eventually elects a new leader.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m4p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Producers, MaxQueue, MaxCount

VARIABLES queue, submitted, record, instanceUp

vars == <<queue, submitted, record, instanceUp>>

\* How many of region p's requests currently sit in the shared queue.
CountQueued(p, s) == Cardinality({k \in 1..Len(s) : s[k] = p})

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Producers)
    /\ Len(queue) <= MaxQueue
    /\ submitted \in [Producers -> 0..MaxCount]
    /\ record \in [Producers -> 0..MaxCount]
    /\ instanceUp \in [Producers -> BOOLEAN]

\* No lost updates: every request a region ever submits is eventually applied
\* exactly once -- it is always either waiting in the shared queue or already
\* folded into that region's field of the shared status record, never both,
\* never neither (counted modulo the rolling window MaxCount+1).
NoLostUpdates ==
    \A p \in Producers :
        (record[p] + CountQueued(p, queue)) % (MaxCount + 1) = submitted[p]

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ submitted = [p \in Producers |-> 0]
    /\ record = [p \in Producers |-> 0]
    /\ instanceUp = [p \in Producers |-> TRUE]

\* Backpressure: submission is only possible while the shared queue has room.
Submit(p) ==
    /\ instanceUp[p]
    /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, p)
    /\ submitted' = [submitted EXCEPT ![p] = (submitted[p] + 1) % (MaxCount + 1)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, instanceUp>>

\* The single applier drains the queue strictly in submission order.
Apply ==
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ LET p == Head(queue) IN
         record' = [record EXCEPT ![p] = (record[p] + 1) % (MaxCount + 1)]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<submitted, instanceUp>>

ShutDown(p) ==
    /\ instanceUp[p]
    /\ instanceUp' = [instanceUp EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, submitted, record>>

Restart(p) ==
    /\ ~instanceUp[p]
    /\ instanceUp' = [instanceUp EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, submitted, record>>

Next ==
    \/ Apply
    \/ \E p \in Producers : Submit(p) \/ ShutDown(p) \/ Restart(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
This spec models a power-grid load shedder serving two independent regional controllers, Region A and Region B, that both submit shed-load requests into a single bounded work queue shared by the whole grid (the twist: two independent instances share one pool, here the one queue). Each region's controller can go administratively offline (a planned outage or a communications fault) and later come back online. The full action set is: Submit(p), where an online region p appends a tagged shed-load request to the shared queue, but only when the queue has not yet reached its capacity -- once the queue is full, backpressure blocks further submissions from either region until room opens up; Apply, where the request at the head of the shared queue is popped and folded into that region's field of the shared grid status record, exactly once, in submission order; ShutDown(p), where a region's controller goes offline and stops being able to submit new requests, without touching whatever it has already queued or recorded; and Restart(p), where an offline region's controller comes back online and resumes being able to submit. Because every request that is ever appended is popped and applied exactly once, and only ever in the order it was submitted, no region's shed-load update can ever be silently dropped, duplicated, or overwritten by the other region's update to the shared record.

---- MODULE W4Od13m3p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxQ, MaxCount, MaxTerm, None

ASSUME None \notin Machines

VARIABLES leader, term, downMachine, queue, submitted, ledger

vars == <<leader, term, downMachine, queue, submitted, ledger>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Machines \cup {None}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ downMachine \in Machines \cup {None}
    /\ queue \in Seq(Machines)
    /\ Len(queue) <= MaxQ
    /\ submitted \in 0..MaxCount
    /\ ledger \in 0..MaxCount

\* No lost updates: the ledger's applied count plus everything still pending
\* in the queue always accounts for every request ever submitted so far
\* (counted modulo the rolling window MaxCount+1) -- nothing lost, nothing doubled.
NoLostUpdates == (ledger + Len(queue)) % (MaxCount + 1) = submitted

Init ==
    /\ leader = CHOOSE m \in Machines : TRUE
    /\ term = 1
    /\ downMachine = None
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ submitted = 0
    /\ ledger = 0

\* A functioning machine files a vend request into the shared pending queue.
Enqueue(m) ==
    /\ m # downMachine
    /\ Len(queue) < MaxQ
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, m)
    /\ submitted' = (submitted + 1) % (MaxCount + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, downMachine, ledger>>

\* Only the current leader ever applies, one request at a time, in order.
Apply ==
    /\ leader # None
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ ledger' = (ledger + 1) % (MaxCount + 1)
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, downMachine, submitted>>

\* At most one silent crash ever: the leader goes dark with no warning.
CrashLeader ==
    /\ downMachine = None
    /\ leader # None
    /\ downMachine' = leader
    /\ leader' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, queue, submitted, ledger>>

\* Failover: with no leader, the surviving machines elect a replacement.
Elect ==
    /\ leader = None
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ \E m \in Machines \ {downMachine} :
         /\ leader' = m
         /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<downMachine, queue, submitted, ledger>>

Next == (\E m \in Machines : Enqueue(m)) \/ Apply \/ CrashLeader \/ Elect

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Elect)

\* Once the sole possible crash leaves the network leaderless, it recovers.
Recovery == (downMachine # None) ~> (leader # None)

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2, m3}
    MaxQ = 2
    MaxCount = 3
    MaxTerm = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
PROPERTY Recovery
nl:
This spec models a small network of vending machines that share one central restock ledger. Exactly one machine at a time is the elected leader responsible for applying vend transactions to the ledger; the others merely submit vend requests into a shared pending queue for the leader to process in order. At most one machine in the network can ever crash silently over the whole run (a single, permanent hardware fault with no advance warning), after which the network must fail over to a new leader chosen from the machines still functioning. The full action set is: Enqueue(m), where a functioning machine m appends a tagged vend request to the shared pending queue, as long as the queue has not reached its capacity; Apply, where the current leader pops the request at the head of the shared pending queue and folds it into the shared ledger, in the exact order requests were submitted; CrashLeader, which fires at most once across the whole run and models the current leader silently going dark: it stops being leader immediately, with no other machine told why; and Elect, which fires whenever there is currently no leader, choosing a new leader from among the machines that have not crashed (bumping an election term counter each time). Because every enqueued request is popped and applied exactly once and strictly in submission order, and applying never happens out of order or twice, no vend request's effect on the shared ledger is ever lost, skipped, or double-applied, even across the leader failover caused by the silent crash.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The ledger's value plus the number of requests still waiting in the shared pending queue must always equal the total number of vend requests submitted so far, counted modulo the rolling window, so no submitted update to the shared ledger is ever lost or duplicated.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: After the network's one possible leader crash leaves it without a leader, the network eventually elects a new leader.

---- MODULE W4Od11m1p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumPrinters, Jobs

Printers == 1..NumPrinters
\* The ring order: the printer after p, wrapping back to the first.
Succ(p) == IF p = NumPrinters THEN 1 ELSE p + 1

VARIABLES tokenHolder, printed, voided, released

vars == <<tokenHolder, printed, voided, released>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ tokenHolder \in Printers
    /\ printed \subseteq Jobs
    /\ voided \subseteq Jobs
    /\ released \subseteq Jobs

\* A printed job was never voided, and every printed job had actually been
\* released from the backlog first -- the one irreversible step (printing)
\* only ever happens to a job in good standing, and only once.
Consistency ==
    \A j \in Jobs :
        /\ ~(j \in printed /\ j \in voided)
        /\ (j \in printed => j \in released)

Init ==
    /\ tokenHolder = 1
    /\ printed = {}
    /\ voided = {}
    /\ released = {}

\* The shop moves a backlogged job into the live spool.
ReleaseJob(j) ==
    /\ j \notin released
    /\ released' = released \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, printed, voided>>

\* Only the current token holder may print, and only once, ever, per job.
PrintJob(j) ==
    /\ j \in released
    /\ j \notin printed
    /\ j \notin voided
    /\ printed' = printed \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, voided, released>>

\* Normal exclusive access rotates around the ring.
PassToken ==
    /\ tokenHolder' = Succ(tokenHolder)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printed, voided, released>>

\* Privileged admin override: seize the token for any printer, out of turn.
AdminSeize(p) ==
    /\ p \in Printers
    /\ tokenHolder' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printed, voided, released>>

\* Privileged admin override: permanently cancel a not-yet-printed job.
AdminVoid(j) ==
    /\ j \notin printed
    /\ voided' = voided \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, printed, released>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : ReleaseJob(j) \/ PrintJob(j) \/ AdminVoid(j)
    \/ \E p \in Printers : AdminSeize(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
    NumPrinters = 3
    Jobs = {j1, j2, j3}

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Consistency
nl:
This spec models a print shop's job spooler shared by a ring of printers. Only the printer currently holding the exclusive access token may pull a job off the shared spool and physically print it, and physically printing a job is irreversible -- ink hits paper and it can never be undone or repeated for that same job. Before a job can be printed it must first be released from the shop's backlog into the live spool, and the shop's admin has a privileged override that can seize the token for any printer out of the normal ring order, or void a job outright before it prints, cancelling it permanently. The full action set is: ReleaseJob(j), where the shop moves a backlogged job j into the live spool, making it available to whichever printer is holding the token; PrintJob(j), where the printer currently holding the token pulls a released, not-yet-voided job j from the spool and physically prints it, permanently marking it printed; PassToken, where the token moves from the current holder to the next printer in ring order, the normal way exclusive access rotates; AdminSeize(p), where the admin overrides the ring and hands the token directly to printer p regardless of whose turn it is; and AdminVoid(j), where the admin permanently cancels a job j that has not yet been printed, removing it from consideration so it can never be printed. Because the printed set only ever grows and a job is checked against both the voided set and the released set before it can be printed, no job's physical printing -- the one truly irreversible step in the whole shop -- can ever be triggered more than once, and it can never happen to a job the admin has already cancelled or to a job that was never released from the backlog.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No job that has ever been physically printed was ever voided by the admin, and every printed job had actually been released from the backlog into the spool first.

---- MODULE W4Od7m8p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Yards, Zones, MaxManifest, MaxTx, NoZone, NoSnap

ASSUME NoZone \notin Yards
ASSUME NoSnap \notin (0..MaxManifest)

VARIABLES coarseLock, slotLock, pendingRead, manifest, txCount

vars == <<coarseLock, slotLock, pendingRead, manifest, txCount>>

\* coarseLock is the one shared pool of zone locks both crews contend for.
\* slotLock/pendingRead/txCount are each crew's own independent bookkeeping.
TypeOK ==
    /\ coarseLock \in [Zones -> Yards \cup {NoZone}]
    /\ slotLock \in [Yards -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ pendingRead \in [Yards -> ({NoSnap} \cup (0..MaxManifest))]
    /\ manifest \in 0..MaxManifest
    /\ txCount \in [Yards -> 0..MaxTx]

\* A crew's outstanding snapshot can never be stale: since it can only commit
\* while still holding the exclusive zone lock it read under, no other crew's
\* commit could have slipped in and left it behind the current manifest value.
StalenessOK == \A y \in Yards : pendingRead[y] # NoSnap => pendingRead[y] <= manifest

Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = [z \in Zones |-> NoZone]
    /\ slotLock = [y \in Yards |-> FALSE]
    /\ pendingRead = [y \in Yards |-> NoSnap]
    /\ manifest = 0
    /\ txCount = [y \in Yards |-> 0]

\* Coarse-grained: take the whole-zone lock from the shared pool.
AcquireZone(y, z) ==
    /\ coarseLock[z] = NoZone
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![z] = y]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, pendingRead, manifest, txCount>>

\* Fine-grained: once a zone is held, take this crew's own slot lock.
AcquireSlot(y) ==
    /\ ~slotLock[y]
    /\ \E z \in Zones : coarseLock[z] = y
    /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![y] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, pendingRead, manifest, txCount>>

\* Holding both locks, snapshot the shared manifest to begin a move.
ReadManifest(y, z) ==
    /\ coarseLock[z] = y
    /\ slotLock[y]
    /\ pendingRead[y] = NoSnap
    /\ txCount[y] < MaxTx
    /\ pendingRead' = [pendingRead EXCEPT ![y] = manifest]
    /\ txCount' = [txCount EXCEPT ![y] = txCount[y] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, slotLock, manifest>>

\* Still holding both locks, commit the snapshot back to the manifest.
CommitManifest(y, z) ==
    /\ coarseLock[z] = y
    /\ pendingRead[y] # NoSnap
    /\ manifest' = pendingRead[y] + 1
    /\ pendingRead' = [pendingRead EXCEPT ![y] = NoSnap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, slotLock, txCount>>

ReleaseSlot(y) ==
    /\ slotLock[y]
    /\ pendingRead[y] = NoSnap
    /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![y] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, pendingRead, manifest, txCount>>

ReleaseZone(y, z) ==
    /\ coarseLock[z] = y
    /\ ~slotLock[y]
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![z] = NoZone]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, pendingRead, manifest, txCount>>

Next ==
    \/ \E y \in Yards, z \in Zones :
         AcquireZone(y, z) \/ ReadManifest(y, z) \/ CommitManifest(y, z) \/ ReleaseZone(y, z)
    \/ \E y \in Yards : AcquireSlot(y) \/ ReleaseSlot(y)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ (\A y \in Yards : WF_vars(\E z \in Zones : CommitManifest(y, z)))

\* Every transaction a crew begins (a snapshot it takes) is eventually committed.
Progress == \A y \in Yards : (pendingRead[y] # NoSnap) ~> (pendingRead[y] = NoSnap)

====

CONSTANTS
    Yards = {A, B}
    Zones = {z1, z2}
    MaxManifest = 4
    MaxTx = 2
    NoZone = NoZone
    NoSnap = NoSnap

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT StalenessOK
PROPERTY Progress
nl:
This spec models a container-ship crane yard operated by two independent crane crews, Yard A and Yard B, that both work the same shared set of loading zones. To move a container, a crew must first take the coarse-grained lock on a whole zone (a physical resource shared by both crews -- the twist: two independent crews share one pool of zones), then, once it holds that zone, take its own fine-grained slot lock for the specific spot it is working (each crew's slot lock is its own, independent of the other crew's). Holding both locks lets a crew safely read and update the shared yard manifest, a running count of containers moved yard-wide, without ever stepping on the other crew's update. The full action set is: AcquireZone(y,z), where crew y takes the coarse zone lock on zone z, but only if no crew currently holds it; AcquireSlot(y), where crew y, already holding some zone, takes its own fine slot lock so it can start work there; ReadManifest(y,z), where crew y, holding both its zone lock on z and its slot lock, takes a snapshot of the shared manifest's current value to begin a move transaction; CommitManifest(y,z), where crew y, still holding both locks, writes back its snapshot plus one to the shared manifest, completing the transaction; ReleaseSlot(y), where crew y gives up its slot lock once it has no move transaction still pending; and ReleaseZone(y,z), where crew y gives up the coarse zone lock on z once its slot lock is already free, returning the zone to the shared pool for the other crew. Because a crew can only commit while still holding the exclusive zone lock it read the snapshot under, its write can never be based on a stale snapshot that some other pending write would clobber.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a crew has an outstanding manifest snapshot pending, that snapshot's value can never be behind the shared manifest's current value.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every manifest update transaction that a crew begins is eventually committed.

---- MODULE W4Od5m6p4t1 ----
\* A matchmaker assigns players into a capacity-bounded game lobby using
\* lease-based ownership: a granted slot expires at a bounded clock value
\* and is then reclaimed. Join requests sit in an unordered inbox (a set,
\* not a queue) so the matchmaker may service them in any order relative
\* to when they were sent, modeling a network that can reorder messages.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, MaxCapacity, LeaseDuration, MaxTime

ASSUME /\ MaxCapacity \in Nat /\ MaxCapacity > 0
       /\ LeaseDuration \in Nat /\ LeaseDuration > 0
       /\ MaxTime \in Nat /\ MaxTime > 0
       /\ IsFiniteSet(Players)

VARIABLES lobby, leaseExpiry, clock, inbox

vars == <<lobby, leaseExpiry, clock, inbox>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ lobby \subseteq Players
  /\ leaseExpiry \in [Players -> 0..MaxTime]
  /\ clock \in 0..MaxTime
  /\ inbox \subseteq Players

Init ==
  /\ lobby = {}
  /\ leaseExpiry = [p \in Players |-> 0]
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ inbox = {}

\* A player's join request is dropped into the unordered inbox.
SendJoin(p) ==
  /\ p \notin lobby
  /\ p \notin inbox
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, leaseExpiry, clock>>

\* The matchmaker may service ANY pending request in the inbox, not
\* necessarily in send order -- this is where reordering is modeled.
ProcessJoin(p) ==
  /\ p \in inbox
  /\ p \notin lobby
  /\ Cardinality(lobby) < MaxCapacity
  /\ lobby' = lobby \cup {p}
  /\ leaseExpiry' = [leaseExpiry EXCEPT ![p] = clock + LeaseDuration]
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* An existing lobby member refreshes its lease before it lapses.
RenewLease(p) ==
  /\ p \in lobby
  /\ leaseExpiry' = [leaseExpiry EXCEPT ![p] = clock + LeaseDuration]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, clock, inbox>>

\* A lapsed lease reclaims the slot, freeing lobby capacity.
ExpireLease(p) ==
  /\ p \in lobby
  /\ clock >= leaseExpiry[p]
  /\ lobby' = lobby \ {p}
  /\ leaseExpiry' = [leaseExpiry EXCEPT ![p] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, inbox>>

\* The clock advances, wrapping so it never runs out and stalls the model.
Tick ==
  /\ clock' = (clock + 1) % (MaxTime + 1)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, leaseExpiry, inbox>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Players : SendJoin(p) \/ ProcessJoin(p) \/ RenewLease(p) \/ ExpireLease(p)
  \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: the lobby, which is lease-granted capacity, never exceeds bound.
BoundedCapacity == Cardinality(lobby) <= MaxCapacity

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Players = {p1, p2, p3}
  MaxCapacity = 2
  LeaseDuration = 1
  MaxTime = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
nl:
A matchmaker fills a single game lobby that can hold only a bounded number of
players at once. Players do not join synchronously: each player's request to
join first lands in the matchmaker's inbox, and because the network can
reorder messages, the matchmaker may process any pending request in the
inbox before an earlier one, not necessarily in the order players sent them.
When the matchmaker grants a player a spot, that player receives a
time-bounded lease on the slot rather than a permanent seat: the lease is
stamped with an expiry tied to a shared clock, and a player already in the
lobby may renew that lease before it lapses to keep their seat. If a
player's lease lapses (the clock reaches or passes the stored expiry) before
it is renewed, the matchmaker reclaims the slot, freeing capacity for
someone else. The full action set is: SendJoin, where a player drops a join
request into the unordered inbox; ProcessJoin, where the matchmaker takes
any pending request from the inbox and, if the lobby has room, grants that
player a fresh lease and a seat; RenewLease, where a seated player refreshes
their lease's expiry; ExpireLease, where a seated player whose lease has
lapsed is evicted and their slot freed; and Tick, where the shared clock
advances (wrapping around a bound so the model never runs out of time).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of players simultaneously holding a leased seat
in the lobby never exceeds the lobby's fixed capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m3p1t5 ----
\* A wildfire surveillance swarm elects a leader among its drones; only the
\* live leader may commit a drone's fire-sighting report into the shared
\* status record. Failover re-elects when the leader drops, and a
\* privileged admin action can force a leader in directly. The number of
\* failures is capped so the swarm eventually stabilizes and a leader
\* persists long enough to catch the shared record up to date.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, NoLeader, MaxVersion, MaxFails

ASSUME /\ IsFiniteSet(Drones) /\ Drones # {}
       /\ NoLeader \notin Drones
       /\ MaxVersion \in Nat /\ MaxVersion > 0
       /\ MaxFails \in Nat

VARIABLES leader, up, record, submitted, failCount

vars == <<leader, up, record, submitted, failCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Drones \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ up \in [Drones -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ record \in 0..MaxVersion
  /\ submitted \in [Drones -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ failCount \in 0..MaxFails

\* The freshest sighting version any drone currently holds.
MaxVal(f) == CHOOSE m \in {f[d] : d \in Drones} : \A d \in Drones : f[d] <= m

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ up = [d \in Drones |-> TRUE]
  /\ record = 0
  /\ submitted = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ failCount = 0

\* A drone drops out; at least one drone always stays up, and failures are
\* capped so the swarm cannot be destabilized forever.
Fail(d) ==
  /\ up[d]
  /\ failCount < MaxFails
  /\ Cardinality({x \in Drones : up[x]}) > 1
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
  /\ leader' = IF leader = d THEN NoLeader ELSE leader
  /\ failCount' = failCount + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, submitted>>

\* Ordinary failover: any live drone may step up once there is no leader.
ElectStep ==
  \E d \in Drones :
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ up[d]
    /\ leader' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<up, record, submitted, failCount>>

\* Admin can force-appoint a live drone as leader, bypassing election.
AdminOverride(d) ==
  /\ up[d]
  /\ leader' = d
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, record, submitted, failCount>>

\* A drone produces a fresh sighting, bounded so the model stays finite.
Submit(d) ==
  /\ submitted[d] < MaxVersion
  /\ submitted' = [submitted EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, record, failCount>>

\* The live leader folds the freshest known sighting into the shared
\* record; it never installs anything less fresh than what is already there.
Commit ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ up[leader]
  /\ record < MaxVal(submitted)
  /\ record' = MaxVal(submitted)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, submitted, failCount>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Fail(d) \/ AdminOverride(d) \/ Submit(d)
  \/ ElectStep
  \/ Commit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(ElectStep) /\ WF_vars(Commit)

\* SAFETY: the shared record never reflects more than the swarm has
\* actually reported -- nothing is ever fabricated or regressed into it.
NoLostUpdate == record <= MaxVal(submitted)

\* LIVENESS: whenever some drone has produced a sighting fresher than the
\* shared record, the record eventually catches up to the freshest one.
RecordCatchesUp == (record < MaxVal(submitted)) ~> (record = MaxVal(submitted))

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Drones = {d1, d2, d3}
  NoLeader = NoLeader
  MaxVersion = 2
  MaxFails = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
PROPERTY RecordCatchesUp
nl:
A swarm of drones patrols a wildfire, each one capable of producing its own
fresh sighting of the fire's front. The swarm keeps one shared status record
that is meant to reflect the freshest sighting anyone has produced, but only
the currently elected leader drone is allowed to fold a sighting into that
record. Leadership is normally decided by failover: if the current leader
drops out, any other drone that is still flying may step up and become the
new leader. On top of that, a privileged admin operator can force-appoint
any flying drone as leader directly at any time, bypassing the normal
election entirely, for example to recover quickly from a bad handoff. The
full action set is: Fail, where a flying drone drops out (vacating
leadership if it was the leader), capped so failures cannot destabilize the
swarm forever and at least one drone always keeps flying; ElectStep, where
some flying drone takes over leadership once there is no leader;
AdminOverride, where the admin directly installs a chosen flying drone as
leader regardless of whether one already exists; Submit, where a drone
produces a new sighting of its own, bounded so it cannot report forever; and
Commit, where the live leader folds the freshest sighting the swarm has
produced into the shared status record, never installing anything staler
than what is already recorded.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared status record never shows a sighting fresher
than what some drone has actually produced -- it is never fabricated or
regressed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: the shared status record eventually catches up to the
freshest sighting the swarm has produced.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m7p1t3 ----
\* An elevator bank shares one dispatch record (a version counter plus the
\* current owner) that elevator controllers update via compare-and-swap: a
\* controller must re-read the record before every write attempt, and its
\* write only takes effect if nothing else changed the record meanwhile.
\* A controller may be arbitrarily slow between its read and its write
\* attempt, but it is never removed -- it can always re-read and retry.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Elevators, NoOwner, MaxVer

ASSUME /\ Elevators # {}
       /\ NoOwner \notin Elevators
       /\ MaxVer \in Nat /\ MaxVer > 0

VARIABLES regVer, regOwner, snapshot, committed

vars == <<regVer, regOwner, snapshot, committed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ regVer \in 0..MaxVer
  /\ regOwner \in Elevators \cup {NoOwner}
  /\ snapshot \in [Elevators -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ committed \in [Elevators -> 0..MaxVer]

Init ==
  /\ regVer = 0
  /\ regOwner = NoOwner
  /\ snapshot = [e \in Elevators |-> 0]
  /\ committed = [e \in Elevators |-> 0]

\* A controller refreshes its cached view of the dispatch record. This is
\* always available, so a controller can never be permanently stuck -- it
\* is allowed to be slow, but it is always able to keep retrying.
ReadSnapshot(e) ==
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![e] = regVer]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, regOwner, committed>>

\* The controller's compare-and-swap: the write only lands if the record's
\* version is still exactly what the controller last read. If some other
\* write happened in between, this action is simply not enabled, and the
\* controller must ReadSnapshot again before it can retry.
CAS(e) ==
  /\ regVer < MaxVer
  /\ snapshot[e] = regVer
  /\ regVer' = regVer + 1
  /\ regOwner' = e
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![e] = regVer + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED snapshot

\* The dispatcher can claim the record directly (an emergency recall,
\* say), advancing its version without going through any elevator's CAS.
DispatcherOverride ==
  /\ regVer < MaxVer
  /\ regVer' = regVer + 1
  /\ regOwner' = NoOwner
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snapshot, committed>>

\* Once a claim has been served, the dispatcher clears the current owner.
ClearOwner ==
  /\ regOwner # NoOwner
  /\ regOwner' = NoOwner
  /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, snapshot, committed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E e \in Elevators : ReadSnapshot(e) \/ CAS(e)
  \/ DispatcherOverride
  \/ ClearOwner

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: whenever the record shows a live owner, that owner's own record
\* of its last successful write agrees with the record's current version --
\* an owner is never left crediting an update it did not actually land.
NoLostUpdate == regOwner # NoOwner => committed[regOwner] = regVer

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Elevators = {e1, e2}
  NoOwner = NoOwner
  MaxVer = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
An elevator bank keeps one shared dispatch record describing which car
currently holds the active claim, tagged with a version number. Elevator
controllers do not write to this record blindly: each controller must first
cache a snapshot of the record's current version, and its later
compare-and-swap write only takes effect if the record's version still
matches what it cached -- if the record moved on in the meantime, the
controller's write attempt is simply not accepted, and it must cache a
fresh snapshot before trying again. A controller can be arbitrarily slow
between caching its snapshot and attempting its write -- it is never taken
out of service, so it can always re-cache and retry as many times as it
needs. Separately, the central dispatcher can claim the record directly
(for example, to force an emergency recall), bypassing the compare-and-swap
path entirely, and can also clear the record's current owner once a claim
has been served. The full action set is: ReadSnapshot, where a controller
refreshes its cached copy of the record's version; CAS, where a controller
attempts its compare-and-swap write, which lands only if its cached version
still matches the record's actual current version; DispatcherOverride,
where the dispatcher advances the record's version and claims it directly;
and ClearOwner, where the dispatcher resets the record's owner once a claim
is done.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the dispatch record shows a live owner, that
owner's own record of the version it last successfully wrote always agrees
with the record's actual current version, so no controller is ever left
believing it holds an update that was actually lost.

---- MODULE W4Od4m5p4t1 ----
\* A car-wash conveyor line admits a waiting car onto the bounded-capacity
\* conveyor only once a quorum of station controllers has voted to approve
\* it. Vote messages sit in an unordered inbox and are tallied one at a
\* time in any order, modeling a network that can reorder them. Each car
\* passes through the line exactly once: waiting, on the conveyor, washed,
\* then done.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Controllers, QuorumSize, Capacity

ASSUME /\ Cars # {} /\ Controllers # {}
       /\ QuorumSize \in Nat /\ QuorumSize <= Cardinality(Controllers)
       /\ Capacity \in Nat /\ Capacity > 0

Stages == {"waiting", "onconveyor", "washed", "done"}

VARIABLES state, pendingVotes, tally, slot

vars == <<state, pendingVotes, tally, slot>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ state \in [Cars -> Stages]
  /\ pendingVotes \subseteq (Controllers \X Cars)
  /\ tally \in [Cars -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ slot \in [Cars -> 0..Capacity]

Init ==
  /\ state = [c \in Cars |-> "waiting"]
  /\ pendingVotes = {}
  /\ tally = [c \in Cars |-> {}]
  /\ slot = [c \in Cars |-> 0]

\* A controller sends its vote for a still-waiting car into the inbox.
SendVote(v, c) ==
  /\ state[c] = "waiting"
  /\ <<v, c>> \notin pendingVotes
  /\ v \notin tally[c]
  /\ pendingVotes' = pendingVotes \cup {<<v, c>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, tally, slot>>

\* Any pending vote message is tallied, regardless of send order -- this
\* is where message reordering shows up: tallying need not follow sending.
TallyOne ==
  \E vc \in pendingVotes :
    /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![vc[2]] = @ \cup {vc[1]}]
    /\ pendingVotes' = pendingVotes \ {vc}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, slot>>

\* Once a car has a quorum of votes and a conveyor slot is free, it is
\* admitted onto the conveyor and takes that slot.
Admit(c) ==
  /\ state[c] = "waiting"
  /\ Cardinality(tally[c]) >= QuorumSize
  /\ \E s \in 1..Capacity :
       /\ \A c2 \in Cars : state[c2] = "onconveyor" => slot[c2] # s
       /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![c] = s]
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![c] = "onconveyor"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingVotes, tally>>

\* The car finishes washing and vacates its conveyor slot.
Wash(c) ==
  /\ state[c] = "onconveyor"
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![c] = "washed"]
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingVotes, tally>>

\* The washed car is picked up and leaves the line for good.
Exit(c) ==
  /\ state[c] = "washed"
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![c] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingVotes, tally, slot>>

\* Once every car has finished, the line has nothing left to do; this
\* keeps an action always enabled so the model never deadlocks at the end.
AllDone ==
  /\ \A c \in Cars : state[c] = "done"
  /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E v \in Controllers, c \in Cars : SendVote(v, c)
  \/ TallyOne
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Admit(c) \/ Wash(c) \/ Exit(c)
  \/ AllDone

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A v \in Controllers, c \in Cars : WF_vars(SendVote(v, c))
  /\ WF_vars(TallyOne)
  /\ \A c \in Cars : WF_vars(Admit(c)) /\ WF_vars(Wash(c)) /\ WF_vars(Exit(c))

\* SAFETY: the conveyor never holds more cars at once than its capacity.
BoundedCapacity == Cardinality({c \in Cars : state[c] = "onconveyor"}) <= Capacity

\* LIVENESS: every car put through the line eventually finishes.
AllCarsFinish == \A c \in Cars : <>(state[c] = "done")

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cars = {c1, c2}
  Controllers = {v1, v2}
  QuorumSize = 2
  Capacity = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
PROPERTY AllCarsFinish
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has a fixed number of cars waiting to be washed
and a fixed number of station controllers who must approve each car before
it is let onto the line. A waiting car is admitted onto the conveyor only
once a quorum of controllers has voted to approve it, and the conveyor can
never physically hold more cars at once than its fixed capacity. Votes are
not applied the instant they are cast: a controller's vote for a car is
first dropped into an unordered inbox of pending votes, and because the
network can reorder messages, any pending vote may be tallied before an
earlier one -- tallying does not have to follow the order votes were sent
in. Each car moves through the line exactly once, from waiting to riding
the conveyor to being washed to finally being picked up. The full action
set is: SendVote, where a controller casts its vote for a still-waiting car
into the pending inbox; TallyOne, where any one pending vote is counted
toward its car's quorum, in no particular order; Admit, where a car that
has reached quorum and finds a free conveyor slot is let onto the conveyor
and takes that slot; Wash, where a car on the conveyor finishes washing and
frees its slot; and Exit, where a washed car is picked up and leaves the
line for good; and AllDone, where, once every car has finished and left,
the line simply idles since there is nothing left to do.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of cars riding the conveyor at once never
exceeds the conveyor's fixed capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every car that starts out waiting for a wash eventually
finishes and leaves the line.

---- MODULE W4Od6m2p1t2 ----
\* Two independent elevator-dispatch transactions run two-phase commit
\* against the SAME shared pool of cars. Each transaction picks a target
\* car, tentatively reserves it (prepare), and only then commits the
\* reservation into the pool's permanent ownership record. Because both
\* transactions draw from one pool, prepare must also check the permanent
\* record, not just the tentative lock, or a second transaction could
\* silently claim a car whose assignment was already committed.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Tx, Participants, NoTx

ASSUME /\ Tx # {} /\ Participants # {}
       /\ NoTx \notin Tx

Phases == {"idle", "trying", "prepared", "committed", "aborted"}

VARIABLES txPhase, txTarget, poolOwner, reserved

vars == <<txPhase, txTarget, poolOwner, reserved>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ txPhase \in [Tx -> Phases]
  /\ txTarget \in [Tx -> Participants]
  /\ poolOwner \in [Participants -> Tx \cup {NoTx}]
  /\ reserved \in [Participants -> Tx \cup {NoTx}]

Init ==
  /\ txPhase = [t \in Tx |-> "idle"]
  /\ txTarget = [t \in Tx |-> CHOOSE p \in Participants : TRUE]
  /\ poolOwner = [p \in Participants |-> NoTx]
  /\ reserved = [p \in Participants |-> NoTx]

\* A transaction wakes up and picks a pool resource to try to claim.
Begin(t) ==
  /\ txPhase[t] = "idle"
  /\ \E p \in Participants :
       /\ txTarget' = [txTarget EXCEPT ![t] = p]
  /\ txPhase' = [txPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "trying"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolOwner, reserved>>

\* Prepare phase: the tentative lock AND the permanent pool record must
\* both be free, since the pool is shared with the other transaction.
Prepare(t) ==
  /\ txPhase[t] = "trying"
  /\ IF reserved[txTarget[t]] = NoTx /\ poolOwner[txTarget[t]] = NoTx
     THEN /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![txTarget[t]] = t]
          /\ txPhase' = [txPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "prepared"]
     ELSE /\ reserved' = reserved
          /\ txPhase' = [txPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolOwner, txTarget>>

\* Commit phase: the tentative lock becomes the permanent pool record.
Commit(t) ==
  /\ txPhase[t] = "prepared"
  /\ reserved[txTarget[t]] = t
  /\ poolOwner' = [poolOwner EXCEPT ![txTarget[t]] = t]
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![txTarget[t]] = NoTx]
  /\ txPhase' = [txPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED txTarget

\* A transaction may also voluntarily abort while merely prepared,
\* releasing its tentative lock without ever touching the pool record.
Abort(t) ==
  /\ txPhase[t] = "prepared"
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![txTarget[t]] = NoTx]
  /\ txPhase' = [txPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolOwner, txTarget>>

\* A finished transaction resets so it can attempt a new dispatch later;
\* committed pool assignments are permanent and are never touched here.
Reset(t) ==
  /\ txPhase[t] \in {"committed", "aborted"}
  /\ txPhase' = [txPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<txTarget, poolOwner, reserved>>

Next ==
  \E t \in Tx : Begin(t) \/ Prepare(t) \/ Commit(t) \/ Abort(t) \/ Reset(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: a pool resource is never simultaneously tentatively reserved
\* by one transaction and permanently committed to another -- a committed
\* dispatch assignment can never be shadowed or lost to a concurrent
\* reservation drawn from the same shared pool.
NoLostUpdate == \A p \in Participants : reserved[p] # NoTx => poolOwner[p] = NoTx

====
nl:
An elevator bank runs two independent dispatch transactions, each trying to
assign a hall call to a car, but both transactions draw candidate cars from
the very same shared pool. Each transaction follows a two-phase-commit
protocol: it first picks a target car from the pool, then tries to
tentatively reserve it, and only turns that tentative reservation into a
permanent dispatch assignment once the reservation succeeds. Because the
pool is shared between the two transactions, a transaction's prepare step
must check both the tentative reservation table and the pool's permanent
assignment record before it locks a car -- a car that already has a
permanent assignment from the other transaction cannot be reserved again,
even if its tentative lock happens to be free at that moment. The full
action set is: Begin, where an idle transaction wakes up and picks a
candidate car from the shared pool; Prepare, where the transaction attempts
to tentatively lock its target car, succeeding only if that car is neither
already tentatively locked nor already permanently assigned, and aborting
otherwise; Commit, where a transaction that holds a successful tentative
lock turns it into a permanent pool assignment; Abort, where a transaction
that is merely prepared gives up and releases its tentative lock without
ever touching the permanent record; and Reset, where a transaction that has
committed or aborted returns to idle so it can attempt a new dispatch
later, leaving any already-committed permanent assignment untouched.

SAFETY PROPERTY: a car in the shared pool is never simultaneously
tentatively reserved by one transaction while already permanently assigned
to a different transaction, so a committed dispatch assignment can never be
silently shadowed or lost to a concurrent reservation from the other
transaction sharing the same pool.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m6p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Blood-bank inventory tracker: a shared blood-unit ledger is protected by a
\* time-bounded lease. A technician must Grant(hold) a lease before Entering
\* the critical section that edits the ledger, and a lease that outlives its
\* holder's use can be reclaimed by Expire -- but only while nobody is
\* actively editing, which is what keeps the ledger mutually exclusive.
CONSTANTS Tech, MaxClock, LeaseLen

NoTech == "NoTech"

VARIABLES clock, holder, expiry, editing, pending

vars == <<clock, holder, expiry, editing, pending>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
  /\ holder \in Tech \cup {NoTech}
  /\ expiry \in 0..MaxClock
  /\ editing \subseteq Tech
  /\ pending \subseteq Tech

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ holder = NoTech
  /\ expiry = 0
  /\ editing = {}
  /\ pending = {}

Request(t) ==
  /\ t \notin pending
  /\ t \notin editing
  /\ holder # t
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry, editing>>

Grant(t) ==
  /\ holder = NoTech
  /\ t \in pending
  /\ holder' = t
  /\ pending' = pending \ {t}
  /\ expiry' = IF clock + LeaseLen > MaxClock THEN MaxClock ELSE clock + LeaseLen
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, editing>>

Enter(t) ==
  /\ holder = t
  /\ clock <= expiry
  /\ t \notin editing
  /\ editing' = editing \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry, pending>>

Exit(t) ==
  /\ t \in editing
  /\ editing' = editing \ {t}
  /\ holder' = NoTech
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry, pending>>

\* A lease can only be reclaimed when the holder never actually started
\* editing -- reclaiming an in-use lease would allow a second technician in.
Expire ==
  /\ holder # NoTech
  /\ clock > expiry
  /\ holder \notin editing
  /\ holder' = NoTech
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry, editing, pending>>

TickClock ==
  /\ clock < MaxClock
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, expiry, editing, pending>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Tech : Request(t) \/ Grant(t) \/ Enter(t) \/ Exit(t)
  \/ Expire
  \/ TickClock

Fairness ==
  /\ \A t \in Tech : SF_vars(Request(t))
  /\ \A t \in Tech : SF_vars(Grant(t))
  /\ \A t \in Tech : SF_vars(Enter(t))
  /\ \A t \in Tech : WF_vars(Exit(t))
  /\ WF_vars(Expire)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: the ledger critical section never has two editors at once.
MutualExclusion == Cardinality(editing) <= 1

\* LIVENESS: every technician that requests the ledger eventually gets in.
EventualAccess == \A t \in Tech : (t \in pending) ~> (t \in editing)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Tech = {t1, t2, t3}
  MaxClock = 3
  LeaseLen = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT MutualExclusion

PROPERTY EventualAccess
nl:
This models a blood-bank inventory tracker where several technicians share one
paper ledger recording the unit counts in the refrigerator. Only one
technician may edit that ledger at a time, so access is controlled by a
time-bounded lease: a technician first Requests the ledger (joins the wait
list), then some free moment the system Grants them the lease, stamping an
expiry time on it. Holding a valid (not yet expired) lease lets the
technician Enter the critical section and actually edit the ledger. When
finished, the technician calls Exit, which releases the lease immediately. A
technician can be slow to start editing after being granted the lease (they
might be busy drawing blood, answering a phone, etc.) but is never assumed to
fail outright -- if they take too long, a system clock (advanced by the
TickClock action) eventually passes the lease's expiry, and the Expire action
reclaims the unused lease so someone else can be granted it, but only while
the original holder truly never started editing; a lease is never yanked out
from under a technician who is actively mid-edit. The overall action set is:
Request, Grant, Enter, Exit, Expire, and TickClock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one technician is ever inside the ledger's critical
section (actively editing) at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every technician who requests the ledger eventually gets
to enter the critical section and edit it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m3p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Airport baggage router: a rotating leader router assigns scanned bags to a
\* single downstream chute. Its "load" commands travel over a network that
\* can reorder them, modeled as an unordered set of pending commands each
\* stamped with the sending term; a failover bumps the term so the chute can
\* fence off commands left over from a router that is no longer in charge.
CONSTANTS Router, Capacity, MaxTerm

NoRouter == "NoRouter"

VARIABLES term, leader, alive, chuteCount, inflight

vars == <<term, leader, alive, chuteCount, inflight>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ leader \in Router \cup {NoRouter}
  /\ alive \subseteq Router
  /\ chuteCount \in 0..Capacity
  /\ inflight \subseteq 0..MaxTerm

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ leader = NoRouter
  /\ alive = Router
  /\ chuteCount = 0
  /\ inflight = {}

\* A router may crash as long as some other router remains to take over.
Fail(r) ==
  /\ r \in alive
  /\ Cardinality(alive) > 1
  /\ alive' = alive \ {r}
  /\ leader' = IF r = leader THEN NoRouter ELSE leader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chuteCount, inflight>>

Elect(r) ==
  /\ leader = NoRouter
  /\ r \in alive
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader' = r
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, chuteCount, inflight>>

\* The leader posts a load command stamped with its current term; the
\* network may deliver it whenever, in any order, or duplicate the stamp.
IssueLoad ==
  /\ leader # NoRouter
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {term}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, alive, chuteCount>>

\* The chute may pick up any pending command out of order (reordering);
\* only a command still bearing the current term is honored.
ApplyLoad ==
  /\ term \in inflight
  /\ chuteCount < Capacity
  /\ chuteCount' = chuteCount + 1
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {term}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, alive>>

\* A command left over from a router that has since lost the lead is fenced
\* off and dropped instead of being honored.
DropStale ==
  /\ \E s \in inflight : s < term
  /\ LET s == CHOOSE s \in inflight : s < term
     IN inflight' = inflight \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, alive, chuteCount>>

Unload ==
  /\ chuteCount > 0
  /\ chuteCount' = chuteCount - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, alive, inflight>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Router : Fail(r) \/ Elect(r)
  \/ IssueLoad
  \/ ApplyLoad
  \/ DropStale
  \/ Unload

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: the chute never holds more bags than its physical capacity.
BoundedCapacity == chuteCount <= Capacity

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Router = {r1, r2, r3}
  Capacity = 3
  MaxTerm = 4

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
nl:
This models an airport baggage router: several router nodes compete to be the
one active leader that assigns scanned bags onto a single downstream chute
leading to a flight's loading cart. Router nodes can fail (Fail), and as long
as at least one router is still up, a survivor is promoted to leader (Elect),
bumping a term number so everyone can tell which router is currently in
charge. The leader issues load commands (IssueLoad) to the chute over a
network that is allowed to reorder, delay, or duplicate delivery -- a load
command is really just a stamped "go ahead" signal carrying the term it was
issued under, and the chute may pick any pending signal off the network in
any order (ApplyLoad) rather than the order it was sent. Because failover can
leave old signals from a router that is no longer in charge still drifting
through the network, the chute fences them off and throws them away instead
of acting on them (DropStale) whenever their term is older than the term of
whoever leads now. Bags physically leave the chute onto the cart at any time
(Unload), freeing room for more. The full action set is: Fail, Elect,
IssueLoad, ApplyLoad, DropStale, and Unload.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The chute never holds more bags at once than its physical
capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m9p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Pharmacy dispenser: each dispensing slot's occupant is stamped with the
\* configuration epoch it was assigned under. A reconfiguration (new
\* formulary version) bumps the epoch, leaving older records "stale" until a
\* CatchUp reconciles their stamp -- this is the recovery the liveness
\* property below relies on. A privileged admin may bypass the normal
\* request queue and force-assign a slot directly, but only after evicting
\* whatever is already there, so a slot is never claimed twice at once.
CONSTANTS Drug, Slot, MaxEpoch

NoDrug == "NoDrug"

VARIABLES epoch, assigned, pending, lastEvicted

vars == <<epoch, assigned, pending, lastEvicted>>

Rec(d, s, e) == [drug |-> d, slot |-> s, ep |-> e]

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ assigned \subseteq [drug: Drug, slot: Slot, ep: 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ pending \subseteq Drug
  /\ lastEvicted \in Drug \cup {NoDrug}

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ assigned = {}
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ lastEvicted = NoDrug

HoldsSlot(d) == \E a \in assigned : a.drug = d
SlotFree(s) == ~ \E a \in assigned : a.slot = s

Request(d) ==
  /\ d \notin pending
  /\ ~HoldsSlot(d)
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assigned, lastEvicted>>

\* Ordinary allocation: only a pharmacist who requested may take a free slot.
Allocate(d, s) ==
  /\ d \in pending
  /\ SlotFree(s)
  /\ assigned' = assigned \cup {Rec(d, s, epoch)}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, lastEvicted>>

Release(d, s) ==
  /\ \E e \in 0..MaxEpoch : Rec(d, s, e) \in assigned
  /\ assigned' = assigned \ {Rec(d, s, CHOOSE e \in 0..MaxEpoch : Rec(d, s, e) \in assigned)}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pending, lastEvicted>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, pending, lastEvicted>>

\* Privileged path: admin bypasses the request queue entirely, evicting any
\* current occupant of the slot atomically before installing the new one,
\* so the slot is never held by two drugs even for an instant.
AdminOverride(d, s) ==
  /\ LET evicted == {a \in assigned : a.slot = s}
     IN /\ assigned' = (assigned \ evicted) \cup {Rec(d, s, epoch)}
        /\ lastEvicted' = IF evicted = {} THEN lastEvicted
                           ELSE (CHOOSE a \in evicted : TRUE).drug
  /\ pending' = pending \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A slot's record catches up to the current epoch without changing which
\* drug occupies it -- the recovery step the liveness property depends on.
CatchUp(s) ==
  /\ \E d \in Drug, e \in 0..MaxEpoch :
       /\ Rec(d, s, e) \in assigned
       /\ e < epoch
       /\ assigned' = (assigned \ {Rec(d, s, e)}) \cup {Rec(d, s, epoch)}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pending, lastEvicted>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Drug : Request(d)
  \/ \E d \in Drug, s \in Slot : Allocate(d, s)
  \/ \E d \in Drug, s \in Slot : Release(d, s)
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E d \in Drug, s \in Slot : AdminOverride(d, s)
  \/ \E s \in Slot : CatchUp(s)

Fairness == \A s \in Slot : WF_vars(CatchUp(s))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: a slot is never occupied by two different drug records at once.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A a1, a2 \in assigned : a1.slot = a2.slot => a1 = a2

Stale(s) == \E d \in Drug, e \in 0..MaxEpoch : Rec(d, s, e) \in assigned /\ e < epoch

\* LIVENESS: a slot's stamp that falls behind the current epoch is always
\* eventually reconciled (caught up) or vacated.
EventualReconciliation == \A s \in Slot : Stale(s) ~> ~Stale(s)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Drug = {d1, d2}
  Slot = {s1, s2}
  MaxEpoch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation

PROPERTY EventualReconciliation
nl:
This models a pharmacy prescription dispenser with a fixed bank of dispensing
slots. Each slot's current occupant is recorded together with the
configuration epoch it was assigned under. A pharmacist first Requests a slot
for a drug, and the ordinary Allocate action then hands a free slot to a
drug that requested one, stamping it with the dispenser's current epoch. A
drug already holding a slot is freed up again by Release. From time to time
the dispenser undergoes a Reconfigure (e.g. a new formulary version takes
effect), which bumps the current epoch, and any slot record still carrying
an older epoch stamp is now considered stale even though the drug sitting in
it hasn't changed. A privileged pharmacist-in-charge can use AdminOverride to
force-assign any slot straight to a drug of their choosing, skipping the
normal request queue entirely -- but the override always evicts whatever
occupant is currently in that slot first, atomically, before installing the
new one. Finally, CatchUp reconciles a stale slot record by re-stamping it
with the current epoch without touching which drug occupies it. The full
action set is: Request, Allocate, Release, Reconfigure, AdminOverride, and
CatchUp.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No dispensing slot is ever simultaneously occupied by
records for two different drugs.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a slot's epoch stamp falls behind the dispenser's
current configuration epoch, it is always eventually reconciled to the
current epoch (or vacated).
