---- MODULE W4Od17m8p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

\* Airport baggage router: each conveyor zone holds one shared manifest tally.
\* Updating it is a coarse-then-fine locking dance: a worker takes the zone
\* lock, then the record lock, snapshots the tally into a local cache, and
\* only later writes the incremented value back. Holding both locks for the
\* whole read-modify-write window is what stops a second worker's write from
\* silently clobbering (losing) the first worker's update. Exactly one
\* worker may crash mid-transaction, silently, leaving its locks stranded
\* until an operator force-releases them.
CONSTANTS Worker, Zone, MaxVal

NoW == "NoW"
NoCache == -1

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, val, cache, crashed

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, val, cache, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarseLock \in [Zone -> Worker \cup {NoW}]
  /\ fineLock \in [Zone -> Worker \cup {NoW}]
  /\ val \in [Zone -> 0..MaxVal]
  /\ cache \in [Worker -> (0..MaxVal) \cup {NoCache}]
  /\ crashed \subseteq Worker

Init ==
  /\ coarseLock = [z \in Zone |-> NoW]
  /\ fineLock = [z \in Zone |-> NoW]
  /\ val = [z \in Zone |-> 0]
  /\ cache = [w \in Worker |-> NoCache]
  /\ crashed = {}

AcquireCoarse(w, z) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ coarseLock[z] = NoW
  /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![z] = w]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, val, cache, crashed>>

AcquireFine(w, z) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ coarseLock[z] = w
  /\ fineLock[z] = NoW
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![z] = w]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, val, cache, crashed>>

ReadSnapshot(w, z) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ fineLock[z] = w
  /\ cache[w] = NoCache
  /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![w] = val[z]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, val, crashed>>

\* Writes back the incremented tally and releases both locks in one step,
\* completing the read-modify-write started by ReadSnapshot.
WriteBack(w, z) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ fineLock[z] = w
  /\ cache[w] # NoCache
  /\ val' = [val EXCEPT ![z] = (cache[w] + 1) % (MaxVal + 1)]
  /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![w] = NoCache]
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![z] = NoW]
  /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![z] = NoW]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* Exactly one worker, ever, may crash silently while mid-transaction.
Crash(w) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ Cardinality(crashed) = 0
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {w}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, val, cache>>

\* Operator recovery: reclaim a crashed worker's stranded locks and discard
\* its abandoned in-flight snapshot for that zone.
ForceRelease(z) ==
  /\ coarseLock[z] # NoW
  /\ coarseLock[z] \in crashed
  /\ LET w == coarseLock[z] IN
       /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![z] = NoW]
       /\ fineLock' = IF fineLock[z] = w THEN [fineLock EXCEPT ![z] = NoW] ELSE fineLock
       /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![w] = NoCache]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<val, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Worker, z \in Zone :
       AcquireCoarse(w, z) \/ AcquireFine(w, z) \/ ReadSnapshot(w, z) \/ WriteBack(w, z)
  \/ \E w \in Worker : Crash(w)
  \/ \E z \in Zone : ForceRelease(z)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: the fine (record) lock never outruns the coarse (zone) lock, and
\* any worker with an in-flight cached read still holds the matching fine
\* lock -- together these guarantee the read-modify-write window on a
\* zone's tally is never split open for a second writer to lose an update.
NoLostUpdate ==
  /\ \A z \in Zone : fineLock[z] # NoW => coarseLock[z] = fineLock[z]
  /\ \A w \in Worker : cache[w] # NoCache => \E z \in Zone : fineLock[z] = w

====
nl:
This models an airport baggage router where each conveyor zone keeps one
shared manifest tally (a running bag count for that zone). Updating the
tally correctly requires a hierarchical locking dance: a worker first calls
AcquireCoarse to take the whole zone's lock, then AcquireFine to take the
finer-grained lock on the tally record itself (only obtainable by whoever
already holds the zone lock). Once holding the record lock, the worker calls
ReadSnapshot to copy the current tally into its own local scratchpad, and
later calls WriteBack to write the incremented value back and release both
locks in one step. Holding the fine lock continuously across this whole
read-then-write window is what stops a second worker's write from silently
overwriting (losing) the first worker's update. Exactly one worker, at any
point, may Crash silently while mid-transaction, stranding whatever locks and
cached snapshot it was holding; an operator's ForceRelease action can then
reclaim a crashed worker's stranded zone and record locks and discard its
abandoned snapshot so the zone is not stuck forever. The full action set is:
AcquireCoarse, AcquireFine, ReadSnapshot, WriteBack, Crash, and ForceRelease.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The fine record lock is never held without the matching
coarse zone lock, and any worker with an in-flight cached read still holds
that zone's record lock -- so no worker's read-modify-write on a zone's
tally can ever be split open and have its update silently lost.

---- MODULE W4Od3m3p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Interbank settlement batch: a term-numbered leader bank collects member
\* banks' settlement entries into one clearing batch bounded by a fixed
\* capacity. Exactly one bank, ever, may crash silently (even the leader);
\* failover elects a survivor. Once the leader settles the batch it starts a
\* fresh round, so the system never wedges even after the one crash.
CONSTANTS Bank, Capacity, MaxTerm

NoBank == "NoBank"

VARIABLES term, leader, crashed, batch, settled

vars == <<term, leader, crashed, batch, settled>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ leader \in Bank \cup {NoBank}
  /\ crashed \subseteq Bank
  /\ batch \subseteq Bank
  /\ settled \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ leader = NoBank
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ batch = {}
  /\ settled = FALSE

\* Exactly one bank, ever, may crash silently -- whether or not it leads.
Crash(b) ==
  /\ Cardinality(crashed) = 0
  /\ b \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {b}
  /\ leader' = IF b = leader THEN NoBank ELSE leader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, batch, settled>>

Elect(b) ==
  /\ leader = NoBank
  /\ b \notin crashed
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader' = b
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, batch, settled>>

Submit(b) ==
  /\ leader # NoBank
  /\ ~settled
  /\ b \notin crashed
  /\ b \notin batch
  /\ Cardinality(batch) < Capacity
  /\ batch' = batch \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, crashed, settled>>

Settle ==
  /\ leader # NoBank
  /\ ~settled
  /\ settled' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, crashed, batch>>

\* The leader opens the next clearing round once the current one has closed.
NewRound ==
  /\ leader # NoBank
  /\ settled
  /\ settled' = FALSE
  /\ batch' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bank : Crash(b) \/ Elect(b) \/ Submit(b)
  \/ Settle
  \/ NewRound

ElectAny == \E b \in Bank : Elect(b)

Fairness ==
  /\ WF_vars(ElectAny)
  /\ WF_vars(Settle)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: the clearing batch never admits more member banks than capacity.
BoundedCapacity == Cardinality(batch) <= Capacity

\* LIVENESS: despite the one possible silent crash, the batch always
\* eventually gets settled by whichever bank ends up leading.
EventualSettlement == <>settled

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Bank = {b1, b2, b3}
  Capacity = 2
  MaxTerm = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BoundedCapacity

PROPERTY EventualSettlement
nl:
This models a bank's interbank settlement batch: several member banks feed
their settlement entries into one clearing batch run by whichever bank
currently leads the round, and the leader role is protected by a term-
numbered election with failover. Any bank -- even the current leader -- may
Crash silently at most once across the whole run; if the crashed bank was
leading, its leader slot is vacated. Whenever the leader slot is empty and a
surviving bank is available, Elect promotes that bank to lead and bumps the
term. While a leader is in charge and the current round is still open,
member banks call Submit to add their settlement entry to the batch, but the
batch can never grow past the clearing capacity. The leader calls Settle to
close out and finalize the current batch, and once closed, NewRound reopens
a fresh, empty batch for the next clearing cycle under the same leader. The
full action set is: Crash, Elect, Submit, Settle, and NewRound.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The clearing batch never holds more member banks' entries
than its fixed capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Even though one bank may crash silently at any point, the
settlement batch is always eventually settled.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od17m2p2t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Inst, InitBags, CartTotal

VARIABLES srcCount, dstCount, cartsHeld, phase, pool

Phases == {"idle", "prepared"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ srcCount \in [Inst -> 0..InitBags]
  /\ dstCount \in [Inst -> 0..InitBags]
  /\ cartsHeld \in [Inst -> 0..CartTotal]
  /\ phase \in [Inst -> Phases]
  /\ pool \in 0..CartTotal

Init ==
  /\ srcCount = [i \in Inst |-> InitBags]
  /\ dstCount = [i \in Inst |-> 0]
  /\ cartsHeld = [i \in Inst |-> 0]
  /\ phase = [i \in Inst |-> "idle"]
  /\ pool = CartTotal

\* Prepare: instance i checks a cart out of the single shared pool and loads
\* one bag from its own source belt, entering the two-phase-commit "prepared"
\* state. The pool is shared, so this can starve the other instance.
Prepare(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "idle"
  /\ srcCount[i] > 0
  /\ pool > 0
  /\ pool' = pool - 1
  /\ cartsHeld' = [cartsHeld EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
  /\ srcCount' = [srcCount EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "prepared"]
  /\ dstCount' = dstCount

\* Commit: the destination belt accepts the loaded bag; the cart is released
\* back to the shared pool for either instance to check out again.
Commit(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "prepared"
  /\ dstCount' = [dstCount EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
  /\ cartsHeld' = [cartsHeld EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
  /\ srcCount' = srcCount

\* Abort: the destination belt refuses the bag; it goes back to the source
\* belt, but the cart is still released back to the shared pool.
Abort(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "prepared"
  /\ srcCount' = [srcCount EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
  /\ cartsHeld' = [cartsHeld EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
  /\ dstCount' = dstCount

\* Requeue: a delivered bag is sent back out from the destination belt to the
\* source belt for a connecting flight. This keeps some action always
\* enabled even when the other instance holds the entire shared pool.
Requeue(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "idle"
  /\ dstCount[i] > 0
  /\ srcCount' = [srcCount EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
  /\ dstCount' = [dstCount EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
  /\ cartsHeld' = cartsHeld
  /\ phase' = phase
  /\ pool' = pool

Next ==
  \E i \in Inst:
    \/ Prepare(i)
    \/ Commit(i)
    \/ Abort(i)
    \/ Requeue(i)

vars == <<srcCount, dstCount, cartsHeld, phase, pool>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: bags are never created or destroyed within an instance's own
\* accounting, and carts are never created or destroyed in the pool the two
\* instances share.
BagConservation ==
  /\ \A i \in Inst: srcCount[i] + dstCount[i] + cartsHeld[i] = InitBags
  /\ pool + cartsHeld[1] + cartsHeld[2] = CartTotal

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Inst = {1, 2}
  InitBags = 2
  CartTotal = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BagConservation
nl:
This spec models an airport baggage router that moves suitcases from a source belt to a destination belt using a two-phase commit protocol, run independently for two routing transactions (instance 1 and instance 2) that happen to share a single pool of transfer carts. Each transaction starts with a fixed number of bags waiting at its own source belt. Prepare loads one bag onto a cart checked out of the shared pool, moving that transaction into a "prepared" state. Commit delivers the loaded bag to the destination belt and releases the cart back into the shared pool so either transaction can check it out next. Abort undoes the prepare: the bag returns to the source belt, but the cart is still released back to the shared pool. Requeue recirculates a bag that already reached the destination belt back out to the source belt, the way a bag gets sent back out for a connecting flight; this also guarantees the router always has some action available even when the other transaction is holding every cart in the shared pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For each transaction, the number of bags at its source belt, at its destination belt, and loaded on a cart in transit always sums to that transaction's fixed starting bag count, and the number of carts checked out by the two transactions plus the carts sitting in the shared pool always equals the fixed total pool size.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od17m7p6t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Part, RouteVals, MaxVer

VARIABLES reg, ver, owner, lastSeen, lockdown

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in RouteVals
  /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
  /\ owner \in Part \cup {"admin"}
  /\ lastSeen \in [Part -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ lockdown \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ reg \in RouteVals
  /\ ver = 0
  /\ owner = "admin"
  /\ lastSeen = [p \in Part |-> 0]
  /\ lockdown = FALSE

\* Sync: a handler refreshes their cached version to the register's live
\* version. This read is never blocked by lockdown or by staleness.
Sync(p) ==
  /\ lastSeen' = [lastSeen EXCEPT ![p] = ver]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, ver, owner, lockdown>>

\* CAS: an ordinary handler's proposal only lands if the router is not in
\* lockdown and their cached version still matches the live version (they
\* were not stale). The handler is credited as the route's owner.
CAS(p) ==
  /\ ~lockdown
  /\ lastSeen[p] = ver
  /\ ver < MaxVer
  /\ \E v \in RouteVals :
       /\ reg' = v
       /\ ver' = ver + 1
       /\ owner' = p
       /\ lastSeen' = [lastSeen EXCEPT ![p] = ver + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED lockdown

\* AdminOverride: the privileged admin can force a new route at any time,
\* bypassing both the lockdown and the version-match staleness check.
AdminOverride ==
  /\ ver < MaxVer
  /\ \E v \in RouteVals :
       /\ reg' = v
       /\ ver' = ver + 1
       /\ owner' = "admin"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lastSeen, lockdown>>

\* ToggleLockdown: the admin flips the router in or out of lockdown, which
\* blocks ordinary handlers' CAS proposals but never blocks Sync or override.
ToggleLockdown ==
  /\ lockdown' = ~lockdown
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, ver, owner, lastSeen>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Part : Sync(p) \/ CAS(p)
  \/ AdminOverride
  \/ ToggleLockdown

vars == <<reg, ver, owner, lastSeen, lockdown>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ (\A p \in Part : WF_vars(Sync(p)))

\* Safety: whoever is credited with the current route, if it is an ordinary
\* handler rather than the admin, must not have been stale at the time.
NoStaleOwner == owner \in Part => lastSeen[owner] = ver

\* Liveness: a handler that falls behind the live version always eventually
\* refreshes their cache to match it again.
StaleRecovers == \A p \in Part : (lastSeen[p] # ver) ~> (lastSeen[p] = ver)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Part = {p1, p2}
  RouteVals = {r1, r2}
  MaxVer = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleOwner

PROPERTY StaleRecovers
nl:
This spec models an airport baggage router that keeps a single shared "current route" register (which carousel the next batch of bags should be sent to) alongside a version counter, updated by handlers using a compare-and-swap protocol. Sync lets any handler refresh their locally cached version number to match the register's current version, at any time, for free. CAS lets a handler propose a new route: it only succeeds if the handler's cached version still matches the register's live version (meaning they were not stale) and the router is not in lockdown; on success the register takes the new route, the version advances, and the handler is recorded as the route's owner with their cache immediately updated to match. AdminOverride lets the privileged admin force the register to a new route and advance the version at any time, bypassing both the lockdown and the usual version-match check that ordinary handlers must satisfy -- this is the admin's override power. ToggleLockdown lets the admin flip the router in or out of lockdown mode, which blocks ordinary handlers' CAS attempts but never blocks Sync and never blocks the admin's own override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the current route was last set by an ordinary handler rather than the admin, that handler's cached version must equal the register's live version, so no stale or lockdown-blocked handler's proposal can ever be the one credited with the router's current route.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a handler's cached version falls behind the register's live version, that handler eventually refreshes their cache to match the current version again.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od18m5p6t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Device, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES authorized, devEpoch, epoch, votes, doorState

TypeOK ==
  /\ authorized \in [Device -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ devEpoch \in [Device -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ votes \subseteq Device
  /\ doorState \in {"locked", "unlocked"}

Init ==
  /\ authorized = [d \in Device |-> TRUE]
  /\ devEpoch = [d \in Device |-> 0]
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ doorState = "locked"

\* Vote: a device may only cast a vote in the current round if it is a
\* trusted member of the network and its own clock is not lagging behind.
Vote(d) ==
  /\ authorized[d]
  /\ devEpoch[d] = epoch
  /\ d \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, devEpoch, epoch, doorState>>

\* CatchUp: a slow device (one that has not failed, just lagged) advances
\* its own clock to the network's current round so it can vote again.
CatchUp(d) ==
  /\ devEpoch[d] < epoch
  /\ devEpoch' = [devEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, epoch, votes, doorState>>

\* Unlock: once a strict quorum majority of the network has voted in the
\* current round, the door opens and a fresh voting round begins.
Unlock ==
  /\ doorState = "locked"
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Device)
  /\ doorState' = "unlocked"
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, devEpoch>>

\* Relock: the door can always be manually relocked, independent of the
\* voting round, so the network never stalls once the door is open.
Relock ==
  /\ doorState = "unlocked"
  /\ doorState' = "locked"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, devEpoch, epoch, votes>>

\* ToggleAuth: the network's admin adds or removes a device's trust. Losing
\* trust immediately strikes any vote that device already cast this round.
ToggleAuth(d) ==
  /\ authorized' = [authorized EXCEPT ![d] = ~@]
  /\ votes' = IF authorized[d] THEN votes \ {d} ELSE votes
  /\ UNCHANGED <<devEpoch, epoch, doorState>>

Next ==
  \E d \in Device :
    \/ Vote(d)
    \/ CatchUp(d)
    \/ Unlock
    \/ Relock
    \/ ToggleAuth(d)

vars == <<authorized, devEpoch, epoch, votes, doorState>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: every vote counted toward a quorum in the current round belongs
\* to a device that is both currently trusted and not lagging behind.
VotesCoherent ==
  votes \subseteq {d \in Device : authorized[d] /\ devEpoch[d] = epoch}

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Device = {d1, d2, d3}
  MaxEpoch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT VotesCoherent
nl:
This spec models a smart-home door lock network in which several smart devices decide together, by quorum vote, whether to unlock the front door. The network runs in rounds: Vote lets a device cast its single vote for the current round, but only if the device is currently a trusted member of the network and its own internal clock is not lagging behind the network's round number. CatchUp lets a device that has fallen behind (it is slow, not failed) advance its own clock to match the network's current round so that it becomes eligible to vote again. Unlock fires once a strict majority of the network's devices have voted in the current round: the door opens and a fresh voting round begins with all votes cleared. Relock lets the door be manually relocked at any time once it is open, independent of the voting round, so the network is never stuck waiting on a round while the door sits open. ToggleAuth lets the network's admin add or remove a device's trust; revoking a device's trust immediately strikes out any vote that device already cast in the current round.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every vote counted toward the current round's quorum always belongs to a device that is presently trusted by the network and whose clock is not lagging behind the current round.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od14m5p5t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drone, MaxRound

VARIABLES round, drRound, votes, dropEvents

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
  /\ drRound \in [Drone -> 0..MaxRound]
  /\ votes \subseteq Drone
  /\ dropEvents \in 0..2

Init ==
  /\ round = 0
  /\ drRound = [d \in Drone |-> 0]
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ dropEvents = 0

\* Vote: a drone reports "wildfire confirmed" for the current round, but
\* only if it is caught up to the swarm's current round -- a drone that is
\* still slow (lagging) cannot cast a vote until it resyncs.
Vote(d) ==
  /\ drRound[d] = round
  /\ d \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, drRound, dropEvents>>

\* CatchUp: a drone that has fallen behind the swarm's round (slow, but
\* never treated as failed) resyncs its own round counter to the current one.
CatchUp(d) ==
  /\ drRound[d] < round
  /\ drRound' = [drRound EXCEPT ![d] = round]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, votes, dropEvents>>

\* Drop: once a strict quorum majority of the swarm has voted "confirmed" in
\* the current round, the retardant drop fires. This is irreversible.
Drop ==
  /\ dropEvents = 0
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Drone)
  /\ dropEvents' = dropEvents + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, drRound, votes>>

\* NewRound: while the retardant has not yet dropped, the swarm advances to
\* a fresh surveillance round and clears the current round's votes.
NewRound ==
  /\ dropEvents = 0
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drRound, dropEvents>>

\* Resurvey: the swarm clears out a round's votes to poll again without
\* waiting on the round cap. This keeps the swarm from ever stalling once
\* every reachable drone has already cast its vote.
Resurvey ==
  /\ votes # {}
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, drRound, dropEvents>>

Next ==
  \E d \in Drone :
    \/ Vote(d)
    \/ CatchUp(d)
    \/ Drop
    \/ NewRound
    \/ Resurvey

vars == <<round, drRound, votes, dropEvents>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ (\A d \in Drone : WF_vars(CatchUp(d)))

\* Safety: the irreversible retardant drop happens at most once across the
\* whole mission.
DropAtMostOnce == dropEvents <= 1

\* Liveness: a drone that falls behind the swarm's current round always
\* eventually resyncs to it.
StaleRecovers == \A d \in Drone : (drRound[d] # round) ~> (drRound[d] = round)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Drone = {a1, a2, a3}
  MaxRound = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DropAtMostOnce

PROPERTY StaleRecovers
nl:
This spec models a wildfire drone surveillance swarm that decides, by quorum vote across surveillance rounds, whether to release a fire retardant drop over a monitored zone. Vote lets a drone report "wildfire confirmed" for the current round, but only if the drone's own round counter is already caught up to the swarm's current round -- a drone that is still slow (lagging behind, but never treated as failed) cannot cast a vote until it resyncs. CatchUp lets a drone that has fallen behind resync its own round counter to the swarm's current round, so a slow drone always remains able to rejoin the vote rather than being permanently excluded. Drop is the retardant release itself: it fires once a strict majority of the swarm has voted "confirmed" in the current round, and it is irreversible -- it can only ever happen the one time. NewRound lets the swarm move on to a fresh surveillance round and clear out the current round's votes, as long as the retardant has not already been dropped. Resurvey lets the swarm clear out the current round's votes without waiting for a new round, so a swarm in which every reachable drone has already voted can immediately start polling again instead of stalling.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The irreversible retardant drop happens at most one time across the whole mission.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: A drone that falls behind the swarm's current surveillance round always eventually resyncs to it.

spec_text:
------------------------------ MODULE W4Od6m5p2t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Floor, Elevator, Controller, TotalPax

\* A small recursive fold used to total up a function's values over a
\* finite domain, so the conservation check below is a real sum, not a
\* pair of hardcoded indices.
RECURSIVE SumF(_, _)
SumF(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
       IN f[x] + SumF(f, S \ {x})

VARIABLES waiting, carrying, position, votes

TypeOK ==
  /\ waiting \in [Floor -> 0..TotalPax]
  /\ carrying \in [Elevator -> 0..TotalPax]
  /\ position \in [Elevator -> Floor]
  /\ votes \subseteq Controller

Init ==
  /\ waiting \in [Floor -> 0..TotalPax]
  /\ SumF(waiting, Floor) = TotalPax
  /\ carrying = [e \in Elevator |-> 0]
  /\ position \in [Elevator -> Floor]
  /\ votes = {}

\* CastVote: a controller adds its vote toward the pending dispatch decision.
CastVote(c) ==
  /\ c \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, carrying, position>>

\* Board: once a quorum majority of controllers has voted, an elevator
\* sitting at a floor with waiting passengers may pick one up. The vote
\* pool is spent (reset) once it has been used for a dispatch.
Board(e, f) ==
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Controller)
  /\ position[e] = f
  /\ waiting[f] > 0
  /\ carrying[e] < TotalPax
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
  /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![e] = @ + 1]
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED position

\* AdminBoard: the building's privileged admin can dispatch an elevator to
\* pick up a waiting passenger directly, bypassing the quorum vote entirely.
AdminBoard(e, f) ==
  /\ position[e] = f
  /\ waiting[f] > 0
  /\ carrying[e] < TotalPax
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
  /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![e] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<position, votes>>

\* Alight: a passenger already riding an elevator steps off at whatever
\* floor the elevator currently sits at, rejoining that floor's queue.
Alight(e) ==
  /\ carrying[e] > 0
  /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![e] = @ - 1]
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![position[e]] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<position, votes>>

\* Move: an elevator car travels to a different floor. Always available, so
\* the bank never stalls waiting on a vote or an occupied car.
Move(e, f) ==
  /\ position[e] # f
  /\ position' = [position EXCEPT ![e] = f]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, carrying, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controller : CastVote(c)
  \/ \E e \in Elevator, f \in Floor : Board(e, f)
  \/ \E e \in Elevator, f \in Floor : AdminBoard(e, f)
  \/ \E e \in Elevator : Alight(e)
  \/ \E e \in Elevator, f \in Floor : Move(e, f)

vars == <<waiting, carrying, position, votes>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: no passenger is ever created or destroyed -- every passenger is
\* always accounted for either waiting on some floor or riding some car.
PaxConservation == SumF(waiting, Floor) + SumF(carrying, Elevator) = TotalPax

nl:
This spec models an elevator bank in a skyscraper where dispatch decisions normally require a quorum vote among a small panel of building controllers, except for a privileged admin override. CastVote lets one controller add its vote toward the currently pending dispatch decision. Board lets an elevator car pick up one waiting passenger from the floor it is currently sitting at, but only once a strict majority of the controllers has voted; using the vote pool for a dispatch spends it, resetting it for the next decision. AdminBoard lets the building's privileged admin dispatch an elevator to pick up a waiting passenger directly, at any time, completely bypassing the quorum vote. Alight lets a passenger already riding a car step off at whatever floor that car currently sits at, rejoining that floor's waiting queue (this building's population is a closed loop -- everyone who gets off simply becomes a new waiting passenger). Move lets an elevator car travel to a different floor at any time, regardless of votes or passengers, so the bank is never stuck waiting on a decision.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No passenger is ever created or destroyed -- the total number of passengers waiting across all floors plus the total number riding in all elevator cars always equals the building's fixed total passenger count.
